next_actions.action: Logged the visit for 22 May 2:30pm (tenant at home) and confirmed it to the tenant
Asked Harbour to confirm the visit date (their emails say 21 June) and the fitting date, and to quote before any chargeable work
Told the landlord the oven is out of warranty, that any cost will come as a quote for his approval, and asked about a spend limit
Follow up on 22 May for the visit outcome and quote

boundaries: Booking the visit does not mean the repair is approved or who pays.

remaining_work: Record the work result after the visit (agency, 22 May).
If a quote comes in, record it and request landlord approval (agency).
Landlord to reply on spend limit and approve any quote.
Confirm the visit date and the fitting date with Harbour Services.
missing_info: Landlord spend limit (property record has none)

decision.summary: The oven is not heating. Harbour Services say it is out of warranty, so the landlord's request for a charge-free repair can't be met. I logged the 22 May 2:30pm visit and told the tenant, landlord and contractor. Any chargeable work needs a quote and landlord approval first.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: Contractor is assigned and the visit is booked for 22 May 2:30pm. The oven is reported out of warranty. Outstanding: the inspection result, a quote if needed, landlord approval of any spend, and confirming the dates.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Done now: the visit was logged and emailed to the tenant. Harbour Services were emailed to confirm the dates and to quote before any chargeable work. The landlord was emailed about the warranty outcome. Next: follow up with Harbour Services on 22 May.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: No human decision is needed now. A human or the landlord will only be needed if a quote exceeds authority; the landlord decides on any spend.

actions_claimed.description: Visit set for 22 May 14:30, tenant home

conflicts: The contractor emails say the visit is 'tomorrow, 21st June', but today is 21 May and the call says the next day at 2:30pm. I trusted the call and treated it as 22 May, and asked for confirmation.
Our event 014 email says the oven was replaced in March 2025, which is in the future. The tenant says 'last year'. The fitting date is unverified and I asked the contractor.
The landlord assumed the oven was under warranty. The contractor says it isn't. I trusted the contractor, subject to paperwork.
